newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat refugees expel 100 elderly Serbs.
newsitem.headline: Croat refugees expel 100 elderly Serbs.

text.p: Around 100 elderly Serbs have been expelled from their homes in central Croatia by Bosnian Croat refugees, a human rights group said on Thursday.
Some Serbs were beaten by the Bosnian Croats who included men in military uniform, according to Ivan Cicak, who heads Helsinki Watch in Croatia.
The expulsions took place this week in six villages near Kostajnica on the border with Bosnia southeast of Zagreb.
Cicak said most of the expelled Serbs had lived in the area throughout the 1991-95 war apart from 11 who returned recently from Eastern Slavonia, the last Serb-held region in Croatia.
Kostajnica police chief Zeljko Bolcevic told Reuters that Bosnian Croat refugees had been protesting because they were unhappy with their status.

"There were individual cases of verbal abuse and quarrels with the local Serb population. But there was no organised expulsion," he said. "Some (Serbs) left in fear, but that was not necessary, as we would have protected them as we have done so far."
Three Croats were arrested but later released as the incident qualified only as a misdemeanour, Bolcevic said.
